statement: Put d = 2n. There exist a primitive vector h ∈ Λ with q(h) > 0 and q(h, e) = 0, a rational subspace P = ⟨e, f, v⟩Q ⊂ h⊥ , sign(q|P ) = (2, 1), and a projective semistable family π : Y → ∆ with the following properties. Here ∆ is a sufficiently small disk in a smooth algebraic curve, and ∆∗ = ∆ \ {0}. (1) The total space Y is smooth, the central fiber is a reduced simple normal crossings divisor, and every Yt, t ̸= 0, is an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold in the marked deformation component of X. A line bundle A on Y restricts to an ample bundle on every Yt with c1(A|Yt ) = kh for a fixed positive integer k under parallel transport. The family is the analytic restriction of an algebraic family. (2) The rational vectors can be chosen so that (4.1) q(e) = q(f) = 0, q(e, f) = 1, q(e, v) = q(f, v) = 0, a := q(v) > 0. On the universal cover of ∆∗ the marked Hodge line is spanned by the normalized vector (4.2) p(τ) = f + τv − a 2 τ2 e, Im τ > 0. The function τ tends to the cusp represented by the original line Qe, and (4.3) q(p(τ)) = 0, q(p(τ), e) = 1, q(p(τ), p(τ)) = 2a(Im τ)2 . For a consistent convention for second-cohomology monodromy there is a rational w > 0 such that (4.4) Me = e, Mv = v − awe, Mf = f + wv − aw2 2 e, M|P⊥ = 1. The orthogonal complement in the last formula is taken in ΛQ. In particular, (4.5) (M − 1)P = ⟨e, v⟩Q, (M − 1)2 f = −aw2 e ̸= 0, (M − 1)3 = 0. The same image statement holds if the monodromy convention uses M−1. (3) There is a single-valued holomorphic relative symplectic form σt on the smooth family, uniquely normalized by q([σt], e) = 1. The forms ηt = σn t extend to a holomorphic section of the relative logarithmic top-form line bundle of the semistable family. With s = − log |t|, (4.6) csd ≤ Z Yt |ηt|2 ≤ Csd for positive constants c, C. There is a point o ∈ Y0 where d + 1 components meet and coordinates satisfying (4.7) t = z0 · · · zd, η = F(z) dz1 z1 ∧ · · · ∧ dzd zd , F(o) ̸= 0. (4) For any prescribed irrational number λ, there is a path tending to 0 in ∆∗, with a continuous choice of lift, along which τ = λ + iy and y → +∞.
